owner.occupation: Runs a small experimental electronic music label

world.bio: Ex-sound engineer who now runs a vinyl-only label from a Neukölln basement. The catalogue sits between drone, folk instruments and modular synths: fourteen releases in six years, pressings of 300 to 500, mostly sold out through a mailing list and two record shops. I master everything myself on a lathe-cut setup I borrowed from a friend and then bought from him on instalments.
skills_assets: A basement studio with a modular rack, a small mastering chain and a listening room
Relationships with two pressing plants (Czech Republic and Germany)
Distribution through three European shops and a mailing list of about 2,300
Booking contacts in Berlin, Rotterdam, Ghent and Lyon
Years of experience as a live-sound engineer for festivals
A volunteer slot on a Sunday radio show on a community station

projects.name: Spring compilation: free-reed instruments + modular synths
projects.text: I am planning a compilation of free-reed instruments with modular synths for next spring; I have accordion and harmonium artists, and I am still missing an East Asian reed instrument. Eight tracks planned, two per side on two LPs; I have signed the accordion player from Rotterdam and a harmonium duo from Ghent. The idea came after a Sunday radio guest played a sheng sample and everybody in the studio went quiet.

projects.name: Catalogue 15 master
projects.text: A drone record by a cellist in Leipzig. Mastering session is booked for the second week of October; the plant needs the files by the 25th.

projects.name: Basement damp problem
projects.text: Water on the east wall every autumn. The landlord says it is "normal for a cellar". I have moved the records onto shelves with feet and bought a dehumidifier that sounds like a small jet.

notes.text: Georgian cooking attempt number three. Khachapuri adjaruli. The dough is better, the egg yolk cooked too much. My housemate looked at it and said "it is fine, it is a very brave egg".

Landlord sent the rent increase letter: 18 percent from January. I read it twice and put it in the folder marked "later". Started browsing flats in Wedding and Moabit. Everything is either too small or too far from the U8.

Listened to the harmonium duo from Ghent for the third time today. Their long chord at minute six does something to my chest. The challenge for the compilation is that the instruments all breathe, which is great, but too many breathing things in a row can become soup. I need contrast. I need something that bites. An East Asian mouth organ would be ideal; I have thought about the sheng, the khaen, even a shō. I do not know anybody who plays them seriously with electronics.
Sunday radio show prep. My co-host wants to play only field recordings. I want to play something with a beat. We compromised with a field recording of a drum.
Pressing plant quote for the next record went up 11 percent. Vinyl is a bad business and I love it. A friend at a label in Lyon said she is switching to cassette. I had to go for a walk.
The modular crashed during a patch I had been building for an hour. No recall. I have never been so close to throwing a module out of the window.
Went to a gig at Berghain's smaller room. The sound system is perfect and the crowd talks over the quiet parts. I stood in the back and thought: this is why I run a label for people who listen.
Mother called from Hannover. She asked when I am going to get a real job. I said I have one. She said "a job with a pension".
Rough mix of the cellist's record is done. It is 41 minutes, which is the perfect length for a side-and-a-half. Cut the last three minutes. They were self-indulgent. They were also my favourite.

messages.text: Mara: The dehumidifier is making the noise again. Me: I know, I'm sorry. Mara: It sounds like a jet. Me: It IS a jet. It is also holding off the mould.
Pieter: I can send the stems for the second piece on Friday. Me: Perfect. Is the drone underneath you or is it a separate layer? Pieter: Separate, so you can lower it. Me: Beautiful.
Camille: We are doing the next one as cassette only. Me: Betrayal. Camille: It is 1.20 per unit instead of 6.80. Me: Fine. Betrayal accepted.
Landlord: Please sign the attached letter by 30 September. Me: I will review it with a lawyer. Landlord: That is your right.
Cellist: Is there any chance of changing the sequencing? Me: Show me. Cellist: Put the long one last. Me: I think you are right.

relations.about: Runs a sister label, goes cassette

constraints: Vinyl only, small pressings; no streaming-first release
Cannot pay advances above 300 euros per artist
Needs files from artists by early January for a spring release
Must find a new flat before January because of the rent increase
sensitive: The label is running at a small loss; he covers it with freelance sound work
Fears the rent increase may force him to leave the basement
Mother thinks he wasted his career
